When an agent’s command, tool call or test fails, the useful part of the error is buried in fifty lines of framework internals. Stack Trace puts the error type and message first, shows your own frames in full contrast with file, line and column, and folds every run of framework frames into one quiet row like “8 framework frames · next”.

parseError reads an Error object, including its name, message and cause chain. Show the trace in development and a plain message in production.
parseStackTrace and StackFrames work on their own, for example to show a short stack under each failed test.

parseStackTrace reads V8 stacks from Node, Chrome, Bun and Deno, Firefox and Safari stacks, Vitest frames with the code under them and Python tracebacks, including chained causes from [cause], Caused by: and Python’s “direct cause” and “during handling” sections. It classifies node_modules, node:internal, Next.js internals, site-packages and the standard library as non-app code, and turns file:// and webpack-internal paths into readable project paths. Lines it doesn’t recognise are kept, never dropped.
